target_customer: Business analysts and teams without data science skills who need predictions and data workflows
problem: Business teams need machine learning and recurring data workflows but lack engineers; Intersect automated model selection and later offered data apps and notebooks.
product_category: No-code machine learning and data notebook

founders.name: Aaron Fried
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by TechCrunch in June 2019.

competitors.name: Generable (formerly Stan)
competitors.what: Bayesian modeling for drug discovery, named by TechCrunch as a comparable ML modeling startup

technical_complexity.rationale: Automated model selection and tuning behind a REST API for tabular data is standard AutoML with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: AutoML for single tables was already offered by large clouds and startups, and no data or network moat is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Unknown; YC lists the company as acquired but no acquirer or date was found.

market_need_then: Business teams wanted ML without engineers in 2019, but the launch coverage gives no customer or revenue data.

branding.domain_note: Used intersectlabs.io; the host no longer resolved from the research environment.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, benefit-led taglines such as Machine learning in 3 clicks.

branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt launches in 2019 and Intersect 2.0 ranked number 5 of the day on 2021-08-18.

brand_strength.rationale: Several Product Hunt launches but the generic name Intersect collides with many other companies and no brand press exists.

pivots.to: Data apps and collaborative data notebook for business teams
pivots.why: Not stated; Intersect 2.0 launched as a data app platform in August 2021.

outcome_analysis: Intersect Labs began in 2018 as a no-code machine learning platform, went through YC S19 with a team of four, and by 2021 had pivoted to data apps and notebooks. YC lists it as acquired, but no acquirer, date, price or round could be found, so the story of the exit is not public. With undifferentiated tooling against cloud AutoML and fast-growing notebook rivals, it plausibly ended in a small acquisition rather than a venture outcome, but that is not documented.
notes: Company site intersectlabs.io failed to resolve (dead or blocked); Product Hunt Intersect 2.0 page returned 503. Village.ai lists $150K total raised as seed and StartupIntros lists unrelated Intersect rounds; none verified so no rounds recorded. Acquirer search returned only unrelated Intersect deals (Google/Intersect energy), which are a different company. Competitors listed are the comparables TechCrunch named, which are loose.
